evidence.title: Robinson City Council Meeting Agenda For May 27th
evidence.supports: Shows the council was still at a 'discuss regulating solar farms and wind energy conversion systems' stage on May 27, 2025 (old business), which bounds the moratorium's true original adoption to sometime after this date.
evidence.quote: In “Old Business,” they will discuss regulating solar farms and wind energy conversion systems.

decisions.notes: Could not pin an exact original adoption date. What is confirmed: as of May 27, 2025 the council was still discussing solar-farm regulation (old business, not yet a moratorium vote); by early-to-mid 2026 a moratorium was in place and had already been extended at least once (the undated 'expires March 24' article); and on Sept. 8, 2026 the council agendized another item titled as a fresh 'ordinance adopting' a moratorium (not an amendment), which is the extension the original researcher's Sept. 8, 2026 citation refers to. Because Robinson appears to re-enact a full new ordinance at each renewal rather than filing amendments, and no single news article or ordinance PDF states the very first adoption date, I could not responsibly narrow this beyond 'sometime between mid-2025 and early 2026' within 3 searches. Checked (beyond the evidence above): a bc-web search for '"solar farm" moratorium passed OR enacted OR adopted city council 2024' (no Robinson-specific hit), and CleanPowerDaily's Illinois solar/wind moratorium opposition tracker (cleanpowerdaily.com/opposition-tracker/illinois), which has no Robinson entry. Left date_enacted_iso empty and enacted_status/current_status unchanged; not a REMOVE, since the underlying instrument and its extended history are well corroborated by multiple sources.
